title: Release experiment lattice — canary & A/B framework (WIP)
body:
Purpose
This is a working doc to converge on a lightweight, cross-functional decision lattice for staged releases: canaries, shadowing, and A/B experiments. Goal is to give product, SRE, serving-runtime, and console teams a shared vocabulary and automation hooks so we can ship confidently and scale rollouts without manual firefighting.

High-level principles
- Small, observable changes first: prefer micro-canaries with tight signal windows.
- Safety as default: automated rollback thresholds for latency, error-rate, and quality regressions.
- Ownership and intent: every rollout has a clear owner, hypothesis, metrics, and rollback plan.
- Reuse and composability: build experiment primitives (ramp, shadow, split, cohort) that teams can combine.

Decision lattice concept (quick explainer)
- Input axes: risk (user-impact), novelty (model change magnitude), exposure (traffic %, endpoint criticality).
- Output axes: rollout pattern (shadow -> canary -> ramp -> global), monitoring scope (per-token vs request), approval path (auto vs manual).
- Example lattice cells:
  - Low risk / low novelty -> short auto-canary (1% -> 5% over 1 hour) with basic latency and errors.
  - High risk / high novelty -> gated rollout with prod-simulated load test, extended canary (0.5% -> 2% -> 10%), manual ops approval, scenic rollback.

Gating signals (core set)
- Safety signals (automated):
  - Request error rate delta (absolute increase > 0.5% or relative > 2x over baseline)
  - Infrastructure errors (OOM, GPU timeouts)
  - Latency regression: p95 increase > 20% or p99 increased > 15%
- Quality signals (model behavior):
  - NLU accuracy or rerank loss on holdout prompts (if available)
  - Regression in eval prompt set: fail if BLEU/ROUGE or embedding-similarity drops by threshold
  - Human-annotated quality checks for initial canaries (sample of 200 requests)
- Business signals:
  - Increase in support tickets or negative CSAT correlated to endpoint
  - Unexpected cost per token > threshold

Metrics and dashboards
- Must track per-route and per-model: requests/s, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, cost per 1k tokens, model-specific quality metrics, and rollout cohort sizes.
- Suggested dashboards: canary summary (all active canaries), per-experiment detail (cohort breakouts), and signal history windowed to 1h/24h/7d.
- Alerting: automated alerts should be scoped to experiment owners and SRE on-call; include experiment id and current cohort allocation in alert text.

Rollout patterns (primitives)
- Shadow: mirror traffic to candidate model, no responses returned. Use to collect quality signals without user impact.
- Probe-only canary: send a small fraction of requests and discard responses, but run full-cost inference to validate infra and memory. Good for infra / kernel changes.
- Fast ramp (auto): 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with automated checks at each step; step window 15m-1h depending on route criticality.
- Slow ramp (manual): 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with manual approvals between phases. Used for large model architecture or quantization changes.
- A/B split: stable vs candidate split with statistical harness; define metrics of interest and required effect size and power before starting.

Statistical guardrails for A/B
- Minimum detectable effect and sample size must be estimated before allocation. Default power 80% and alpha 5% for product metrics; for low-volume critical routes require higher power and longer durations.
- Prefer binomial or t-test depending on metric. We will provide a Jupyter harness in experiments repo to compute sample sizes per-route.

Automation and API surface
- Experiment manifest (yaml): owner, hypothesis, target endpoints, rollout pattern, metrics, signals, notify list, rollback thresholds, linked tickets. Keep small and human-readable.
- API endpoints: create_experiment, set_cohort_allocation, promote_cohort, abort_experiment, get_experiment_status. These map to rollout-service RPCs (see linked PR).
- Console: single pane to view active experiments, force-promote / pause, and inspect raw signals for cohorts.

Playbook checklist (pre-rollout)
- Owner declared and collaborators added to experiment manifest.
- Hypothesis and primary/secondary metrics documented.
- Baseline metrics captured (last 7 days).
- E2E smoke tests and perf tests for candidate model passed in staging.
- Rollback plan and postmortem owner assigned.
- Communication plan: Slack channel + status page update cadence.

Runbook snippets (quick actions)
- Abort and rollback via CLI: rolloutctl abort --experiment EXP-123 --reason "p95 spike"
- Force promote: rolloutctl promote --experiment EXP-123 --to 100
- Pause ramp: rolloutctl set-cohort --experiment EXP-123 --cohort A --percent 0
- Query status: rolloutctl status --experiment EXP-123 (returns JSON with metrics)

Safety-first examples (concrete)
- Small infra kernel change on transformer runtime: probe-only canary for 24h, monitor GPU OOM and p95. If alert occurs, rollback to previous kernel and block next kernel rollout until root cause.
- New quantized variant: shadow + 1% fast-canary for 6 hours with human-in-the-loop sample review. Reject if semantic similarity on eval set drops below 0.92.

Open questions and tradeoffs
- How do we balance quality evals that require human labeling in the canary window? Practically we need a small sample live-annotation workflow.
- Who has final approval for high-risk rollouts: currently thinking product manager + SRE lead signoff. Need legal/security review path for private deployments.
- Can we build a generic sample-scheduler to surface representative requests from production to human raters without privacy leakage?

Next steps (action items)
- Product: finalize manifest schema and required fields (Priya + Aisha) — action by 2026-03-20.
- Eng serving-runtime: add probe-only canary flag to runtime (Marco) — prototype by 2026-04-01.
- SRE: define on-call escalation and alert formatting (Evelyn) — draft by 2026-03-25.
- Devex: console mockups for experiment panel (Samir) — wireframes by 2026-03-18.

Notes to self
- Keep the lattice lightweight. Avoid creating a heavyflow that requires 10 approvals for low-risk changes.
- Start with 3 templates: infra-kernel, model-variant, product-experiment. Templates will cover 90% of use cases.

Related tickets and refs
- JIRA-4321 experiment manifest schema discussions
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-service/pull/789 (initial API stubs)
- Confluence draft: rollout framework and decision lattice

If youre reviewing: please add comments inline for any missing signals or edge cases you care about. This will be our canonical working doc until we merge a more formal spec into Confluence.

-- Priya
